message.description: A developer-facing explanation of what went wrong and how to fix it.
message.example: query is required: the food name to search for, e.g. ?query=greek yogurt.

code.description: A stable machine-readable identifier for the class of failure — build retry logic on this, never on message wording. Current values: invalid_request, unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, not_implemented, payload_too_large, rate_limited, internal_error, upstream_error, service_unavailable, upstream_timeout. Only rate_limited, internal_error, upstream_error, service_unavailable, and upstream_timeout are safe to retry (with backoff) — not_implemented is permanent until the feature ships. New codes may be added over time; treat an unknown code according to its HTTP status class.

docs_url.description: Link to the developer documentation for this API version.

scaling_factor.description: Multiplier applied to the food's nutrition values for this serving.

is_primary.description: Whether this is the default serving for the food.

nutrients.description: Per-serving nutrition in the shared nutrient vocabulary. Keys are omitted when the database has no value.

image_url.description: URL of a picture of the food, when the database has one.

upc.description: The product's barcode, for branded foods that have one.

total_count.description: Total number of matches in the database; may exceed the number of items returned.

name.description: Generic foods are lowercase; branded foods keep their product name.

image_url.description: Thumbnail of the food, when the database has one.

nutrients.description: Calories per default serving, in the shared nutrient vocabulary — the one nutrient a suggestion carries. Fetch the food for the full panel.

items.description: Ranked suggestions, generic foods before branded. Empty when nothing matches.

diet_restrictions.description: Allergens/ingredients to avoid. Omit it (or send []) if none apply.

diet_preferences.description: Dietary patterns to match. Omit it (or send []) if none apply.

CompleteScanNutritionFacts.description: Nutrients reported by analysis and alternatives. Each key may be omitted when not supplied. An absent key is not a measured zero. Present amounts retain their value and unit.

alternatives.description: Healthier alternatives matching the restrictions and preferences. An empty array is a valid result, not an error.

type.description: When coordinates are provided and the name matches no restaurant, results may be menu items instead.

distance.description: Distance from (latitude, longitude) in meters; present only when coordinates were provided.

total_count.description: Total number of matches; may exceed the number of items returned.

nutrients.description: Per-dish nutrition in the shared nutrient vocabulary. Keys are omitted when the menu source has no value.

image_url.description: URL of a picture of the dish, when the source has one.

total_count.description: Total number of matches; may exceed the number of items returned.

image.description: The meal photo, as an http(s) URL or a base64 data URI (data:image/jpeg;base64,…). Any image of the meal works — a camera photo, a screenshot, or a hosted picture. Formats: JPG, PNG, WEBP, and non-animated GIF. A URL must be publicly fetchable server-side: hosts that block hotlinking or require a login cannot be read. Prefer the URL when the image is already hosted — base64 inflates the payload by ~33%, and request bodies over 5 MB are rejected, so keep raw images under ~3.5 MB when encoding.

selected_quantity.description: Quantity the parser selected from the text ('2 cups' → 2); text scans only. Advisory — corrections reads the serving's own quantity.

servings.description: Never empty: every detection producer guarantees at least one serving.

detections.description: Detected foods. Always present — an empty array means nothing was recognized.

text.description: Natural-language description of what was eaten; parsed into detected foods with quantities.
text.example: a bowl of oatmeal with honey and a banana

meal_name.description: The meal name from the scan, when it returned one (photo scans do; text scans don't). Defaults to 'Meal'.

detections.description: The detections array from a photo or text food scan, exactly as returned. Omitted zero-value nutrient keys are filled in automatically; each detection needs at least one serving.

user_input.description: Plain-English description of what to correct.
user_input.example: The oatmeal was steel-cut, about 2 cups, and there was no honey.

quantity.description: How many of that serving were consumed.

timestamp_utc.description: When the meal was eaten — any ISO-8601 offset; stored and returned in UTC. Omitted = now.

serving_details.description: The serving definition the quantity refers to.

timestamp_utc.description: Returned UTC timestamp. Treat as an opaque string because deployed responses are not consistently RFC 3339 formatted.

items.description: Logs in the range, ordered by timestamp. An empty list is a valid result.

timestamp_utc.description: UTC consumption time, ending in Z.

status.description: Deletion is idempotent — an unknown or already-deleted log_id returns the same response.

health_conditions.description: Omit it (or send []) if none apply. Type 1 diabetes is not supported by the prediction model.

value.description: mg/dL. At most one reading per 15-minute window.

foods.description: The meal to predict the glucose response for.

start_time.description: When the meal is (or will be) eaten. Must carry a timezone designator.

cgm_data.description: Optional CGM history for personalization; requires consumed_foods.

consumed_foods.description: The meals eaten during the CGM history; requires cgm_data.

min.description: Suggested Y-axis lower bound (mg/dL). A fixed target-range bound, not the minimum of the curve.

max.description: Suggested Y-axis upper bound (mg/dL): 180 with Type 2 diabetes in health_conditions, otherwise 140. Not the maximum of the curve.

prediction.description: The predicted glucose curve at 15-minute intervals, starting at start_time.

FoodId.description: Stable food identifier, provisionally narrowed to JavaScript's safe integer range.

ServingId.description: Stable serving identifier, provisionally narrowed to JavaScript's safe integer range.

FoodLogId.description: Stable food-log identifier; the upstream 400 response explicitly rejects non-UUID values.

PartnerUserId.description: Stable partner-owned identifier of the end user for whom a request is made.

Barcode.description: A 6-to-14-digit UPC, EAN, or GTIN barcode; represented as a string to preserve leading zeroes.

ConfidenceScore.description: Photo scans only; absent on text scans.

Sex.description: Biological sex, as consumed by the prediction model.

message.description: A developer-facing explanation of what went wrong and how to fix it.
message.example: query is required: the food name to search for, e.g. ?query=greek yogurt.

code.description: A stable machine-readable identifier for the class of failure — build retry logic on this, never on message wording. Current values: invalid_request, unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, not_implemented, payload_too_large, rate_limited, internal_error, upstream_error, service_unavailable, upstream_timeout. Only rate_limited, internal_error, upstream_error, service_unavailable, and upstream_timeout are safe to retry (with backoff) — not_implemented is permanent until the feature ships. New codes may be added over time; treat an unknown code according to its HTTP status class.

token.description: The credential itself. Shown exactly once — it is stored only as a hash and can never be retrieved again.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires, counted from the moment this response was produced. Compute expiry from this rather than from `expires_at` — a device clock that is wrong makes an absolute timestamp wrong with it.

expires_at.description: The same expiry as an absolute UTC instant, for logs and humans.

end_user_id.description: The end user this token is bound to, echoed back so a caller can assert it minted what it meant to.

scopes.description: What this token may do — the scopes granted, whether requested explicitly or defaulted.

end_user_id.description: Your stable ID for the end user this token acts as. The token is bound to it; requests made with the token act only on this user.

scopes.description: What the token may do. Omit to grant the full client-grantable set (foods:read, food_scans:write, food_logs:read, food_logs:write, glucose:read, restaurants:read). Grant only what the screen needs.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the token stays valid, in seconds. Between 300 and 7200; defaults to 1800.

plan.description: The plan this allowance comes from.

period_start.description: First day of the current billing period (UTC), inclusive.

period_end.description: Last day of the current billing period (UTC), inclusive.

resets_at.description: When the allowance resets and `used_credits` returns to 0.

included_credits.description: Credits included in the plan for this period. Absent when the plan has no ceiling.

used_credits.description: Credits used so far this period. One successful v1.2 API call costs 1 credit; failed calls cost nothing.

remaining_credits.description: Credits left in this period. Absent when the plan has no ceiling.
